1.title: Weston Consulting Notice
1.content: This is the Consultation Notice project.
1.subtitle: Designing Accessible Public Consultation Notices that Engage Communities.
1.overview:
As part of Weston Consulting's Community Consultation initiatives, this project aimed to redesign the Public Consultation Notice a document distributed to residents within designated city areas to inform them about upcoming developments. 

The new design needed to be modern, approachable, and fully compliant with AODA accessibility standards, ensuring every resident—regardless of ability—could clearly understand the information. Printed on recyclable stock and mailed directly to households, the piece established a new benchmark for clarity, inclusivity, and civic communication design.

8.title: Designing a Green Standards Toolkit for Sustainable & Accessible Urban Practice
8.content: This is the Green Standards Toolkit project.
8.subtitle: Weston Consulting
8.overview:
The Green Standards Toolkit is a guide created to promote sustainable urban development through clear, engaging design. Developed in collaboration with a senior urban designer and an architect, the toolkit communicates complex ideas through layered diagrams, strategic layouts, and accessible formatting, all aligned with AODA standards to ensure broad usability. 

As part of Weston Consulting’s initiative to unify its sustainable design practice, the Green Standards Toolkit was developed to guide internal teams of architects and urban designers toward a shared visual and technical language. This manual consolidates sustainable design standards, principles, and technical drawing conventions into a single, accessible framework, making it easier for teams to maintain visual consistency, clarity, and compliance across all projects.

context.text:
The Green Standards Toolkit transforms dense technical documentation into a visually cohesive and accessible system for sustainable urban design. 

Serving as both a reference and a teaching guide, it standardizes how Weston’s teams communicate concepts, from technical drawing conventions to visual language and accessibility integration, ensuring clarity and consistency across disciplines.
bullets: Developed a unified urban design and architectural language for internal use
Collaborated with architect and urban designer to create 3D and technical diagrams
Ensured full AODA accessibility compliance across print and digital formats
Established drawing and graphic consistency standards now used company-wide

8.problem: With the team producing multiple technical drawings and planning documents, the company needed a unified approach to maintain visual quality, accessibility, and sustainability alignment. We were tasked to create a toolkit that simplifies communication, and standardize visual output.
8.research: The layout was structured using accessible typography, a clear visual hierarchy, and a modular template to ensure consistency and efficient rollout. Visual elements, including a custom-designed map, were created to meet accessibility guidelines and enhance clarity. Integrated QR codes allow for extended digital engagement, and the final piece was printed on recyclable stock, reinforcing sustainable design practices.
8.process: Designing a toolkit that draws connection between disciplines.
8.solution: A unified visual and technical framework for sustainable design. The final Green Standards Toolkit establishes a shared design language that aligns technical drawing standards, accessibility principles, and sustainable design guidelines. It functions as both a visual system and a technical manual, ensuring that every diagram, layout, and illustration across Weston Consulting reflects clarity, sustainability, and compliance.
8.impact: The layout was structured using accessible typography, a clear visual hierarchy, and a modular template to ensure consistency and efficient rollout. Visual elements, including a custom-designed map, were created to meet accessibility guidelines and enhance clarity. Integrated QR codes allow for extended digital engagement, and the final piece was printed on recyclable stock, reinforcing sustainable design practices.
results: A visually cohesive toolkit praised for its clarity, colour use and accessibility
Full AODA compliance achieved through careful typographic, color, and layout decisions
Seamless integration of custom diagrams and content, resulting in an engaging user experience
Successfully supported interdisciplinary collaboration in communicating sustainable planning practices
technologies: Design: Adobe InDesign, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Procreate
Accessibility & Standards: AODA, WCAG 2.1, Ontario Building Code
Visualization: AutoCAD (3D modeling, in collaboartion with Architect)
